title: Final Environmental Impact Assessment before Decision on Alignment Option for Cross Island MRT Line
what_it_is: Final Environmental Impact Assessment before Decision on Alignment Option for Cross Island MRT Line

sections.label: Phase 1 EIA findings
sections.summary: Phase 1 of the EIA found site investigation works could proceed with moderate impact on few parts of the nature reserve, with mitigating measures and controlled access.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Findings from Phase 1 of the EIA concluded that the site investigation works, with the implementation of mitigating measures and controlled access, could be carried out with moderate impact on the few parts of the nature reserve where these works were to take place.

sections.label: Phase 2 EIA findings
sections.summary: Phase 2 of the EIA took three years, was gazetted in September 2019, and concluded both underground alignment options are feasible with appropriate mitigating measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Phase 2 of the EIA took a further three years and the findings were gazetted in September 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The report concluded that both underground alignment options are feasible with appropriate mitigating measures.

sections.label: Feedback and mitigation measures
sections.summary: Feedback helped LTA develop comprehensive measures to mitigate potential impact during construction and operation of the CRL, and there are no plans for a further EIA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Their feedback has helped LTA develop a comprehensive set of measures to mitigate the potential impact during the construction and operation of the CRL.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: There are no plans for a further EIA.

sections.label: Holistic impact ecosystem valuation
sections.summary: The member asks whether a more holistic valuation of the worksite environment has been done or is prepared, using ecosystem service valuation techniques assessing economic, cultural and environmental value of natural capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Perhaps, let me explain further about my second supplementary question in terms of what I mean by "holistic impact".

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: I am asking if we have done, and if not, are we prepared to do a more holistic valuation of the worksite environment through ecosystem service valuation techniques which assess the economic, cultural and environmental value of our natural capital.

sections.label: Clarification on considering valuation information
sections.summary: The member seeks clarification on whether these are prepared to be considered if not done, as useful information for aligning the CRL, though not the only factor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: But I am just asking for clarification whether they are prepared to consider these, if these have not been done.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It is a useful set of information for us to then consider how best to align the CRL.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It is not the only factor that is taken into account.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, in making the decision, economic and many other factors will have to be taken into account.
